森の家.name: Mori no Ie
森の家.desc: A shop tucked quietly away in the forest of Izumi. Look for the arched gate guarded by shisa and the handmade mailbox. The everything-on-top "Mix Soba" is a big-volume bowl with pig's feet (tebichi), pork spare ribs (soki), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and a boiled egg. Great for a drive in cherry blossom season, too.
t: *This article was created with AI (ChatGPT 5.1 Thinking) and partly added to by me 😆

I ate here in February 2025 😄　As you drive up the winding road toward the mountains of Izumi in Motobu Town, the surroundings are nothing but forest, to the point where you get a little nervous wondering, "Is there really a shop up ahead…?" 🌿　Along the way the Taiwan cherry blossoms happened to be in bloom, deep pink puffs floating up here and there, a view that made me want to stop the car and just gaze at it 🌸　Appearing quietly in the middle of that forest is the Okinawa soba shop I visited this time, "Mori no Ie".
Mori no Ie (it's seriously in the middle of the forest 😆)
Mori no Ie (it's seriously in the middle of the forest 😆)
Mori no Ie (it's seriously in the middle of the forest 😆)
Cherry blossoms along the road near the shop lol
Cherry blossoms along the road near the shop lol

Walking toward the shop, the first thing that catches your eye is an arched gate guarded by shisa. The stone paving underfoot has a swirling pattern, and it somehow feels like you've wandered into a secret garden 🙂　The surroundings are full of trees and plants, truly a "house in the forest" just like the name. Next to the entrance sits a colorful mailbox with a very handmade feel, and it was so cute it got me excited 📮
Inside the shop
Inside the shop
Inside the shop
Inside the shop

Stepping inside, there's a glossy wooden floor lined with rattan chairs and wooden tables. Near the ceiling there's a display that makes use of branches just as they are, and in the center there's even a large aquarium. It's a strangely calming space, like a slightly retro coffee shop, a mountain hut and an art space all mixed together.
Menu
Menu

Opening the menu, in addition to the standards like soki soba, braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) soba and pork offal (nakami) soba, there were unusual ones like beef soba and even beef curry soba, which surprised me a bit. There's also a kids' soba, so it seems easy to come with the family. For drinks, they have coffee, tea, fruit juice, and Orion Beer properly on the lineup too 🍺　I hesitated over a lot of things, but this time I ordered the "Mix Soba", which was labeled a "Recommended Popular Menu Item". It's what you'd call an everything-on-top bowl.
Mix Soba (medium)　¥1,000

After waiting a little while, the Mix Soba arrived generously piled in a large bowl. Pig's feet (tebichi), pork spare ribs (soki), braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), a boiled egg, shiitake mushrooms, kelp, green onions… there was so much topping you could barely see the noodles, and the moment I saw it I let out an "Ohhh!" 😆　First, a sip of the broth. It seems to be a blended stock of bonito and pork bone, and the bonito broth really comes through. The shiitake stock is also strong, and it reminded me of the flavor at "Papa Subu" in Ginowan City.
Mix Soba (medium)　¥1,000
The noodles are medium-thick and straight. The texture is not too soft, but not rock-hard firm either, right down the middle.

The meats have plenty of presence, just as they look. The pig's feet (tebichi) were jiggly, and the fat was melt-in-your-mouth ✨　The seasoning on the pork spare ribs (soki) and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) was light across the board. A sinewy texture remains here and there.

The boiled egg topping might be a point unique to this place, too. Rather than a seasoned egg, it's an old-fashioned, firmly hard-boiled egg, with a half plopped right on top, a style you don't see much at other shops, so it felt a little fresh 🥚

The direction of the flavor is, if anything, on the ordinary side. It's well balanced and easy to eat, but I didn't really feel a strong personality or impact like "you can only eat this here!", that's my impression 🤔　But in exchange, the pairing with the location is outstanding. Outside the window, green spreads out everywhere, and when you step outside after eating, time flows leisurely, with only the sound of birds and the wind to be heard.

Rating (9/15): It's ordinary. I think it's the perfect shop for people who want to step a little away from the busy areas in the heart of the tourist spots and slurp Okinawa soba at a relaxed pace in the forest. Dropping by on a drive in cherry blossom season, or deliberately going on a rainy day to soak in this moist atmosphere: enjoying it together with the scenery may be the tastiest way to enjoy "Mori no Ie" 🚗🌳

花村そば.name: Hanamura Soba
花村そば.desc: A shop in Seragaki, Onna Village, along National Route 58. The signature dish is the ¥800 Hanamura Soba with a blended broth of pork bone, chicken, bonito and kelp. Next door is the attached pottery studio "Unna-yaki", where you can enjoy picking out souvenirs like yachimun pottery and shisa. A shop overflowing with Okinawan vibes, where customers on their way back from diving also stop by.
t: *This article was also made with the help of AI (Claude 3.5 Sonnet), and I added to and updated part of it myself lol
I ate here in June 2024 😄

This time I'm introducing "Hanamura Soba" in Seragaki, Onna Village. At this spot with a superb view surrounded by blue sky and sea, I had an encounter with Okinawa soba that soothed both body and soul. 🌴
Hanamura Soba (along National Route 58; the sea spreads out on the opposite side)
Hanamura Soba (along National Route 58; the sea spreads out on the opposite side)

The first thing that jumps out at you is the "Hanamura Soba" sign standing out against the blue sky. Combined with the tropical palm trees, for tourists, it seems the Okinawan mood will already be at its peak right here 🌺

Entering the shop, there's a calm atmosphere where you can feel the warmth of wood. Looking at the menu, I just couldn't help ordering the "Hanamura Soba", which shares its name with the shop and seems to be the signature dish. 🤤
Hanamura Soba (inside the shop)
Menu
Menu (maybe because there are lots of inbound tourists, there's English on it too)

And now, the long-awaited "Hanamura Soba" makes its appearance! 🎉
Hanamura Soba　¥800

First, let's taste the broth. The stock, combining pork bone, chicken, bonito, kelp and more, has a gentle pork bone flavor coming through. Though it's a complex flavor, it's a gentle taste that somehow feels nostalgic. It wraps you in an indescribable sense of happiness. 😌
Hanamura Soba　¥800

Next, let's taste the noodles. The medium-thick straight noodles are just moderately soft. It's a texture typical of Okinawa soba, and they go perfectly with the broth. The glossiness of the noodles lifted with chopsticks is enough to make you swoon. 😍

And pay attention to the toppings too. Both the braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and pork spare ribs (soki) are simmered until tender. The savory flavor of the meat fills your whole mouth. With fish cake (kamaboko) and chopped green onions added, the colors are vivid too. 🥩🥕
To be honest, you might say the taste is "very, very ordinary". But the great location in the tourist area of Onna Village multiplies the appeal of "Hanamura Soba" many times over.

Looking around the shop, it's bustling with tourists. Interestingly, there were also customers still wearing wetsuits, apparently on their way back from diving, enjoying Okinawa soba at the outdoor tables. The ocean side of the national highway is the sea, and because there's planting along the road, you can't see the sea directly from the shop, but the very Okinawan scene made me smile without thinking. 🏊‍♂️😄
Actually, "Hanamura Soba" has one more attraction. Next to the shop, there's an attached workshop dealing in traditional Okinawan crafts. 🏺
The pottery room next to the shop

Even though it's a soba shop, very Okinawan items like shisa and ceramics are lined up crammed into every corner. After enjoying your Okinawa soba to the fullest, I also recommend taking your time to enjoy choosing souvenirs. 🛍️

Rating (9/15): So, how was the Okinawa soba at "Hanamura Soba"? It's a lovely shop where you can enjoy a superb location and Okinawan culture. 😊　Overall, the taste is ordinary, but the great location and the attached workshop are a big draw. 🌊🏺　When you visit on a trip, please do stop by! Nearby there's "Nakamura Soba", which I recommend and have introduced, but if that one is crowded, how about this one instead? I think you can leisurely soak up the Okinawan mood 😄

I lulu cafe.name: I lulu cafe
I lulu cafe.desc: A Thai food cafe along National Route 58. Its specialty is the "Thai-style Okinawa soba", with a pho-like chicken broth topped with shibui (winter melon), chicken thigh and cilantro. You can also change up the flavor with lemon juice, fish sauce and chili. A stylish shop that also sells clothes in the next room.

"I' LULU CAFE" along National Route 58

I'd seen this shop every time I drove along Route 58, but what concerned me was the parking. I'd thought you could park a few cars in front of the shop entrance, but looking carefully this time, it seemed difficult.
So while I was thinking "What should I do?", I noticed something that looked like a parking lot a little way off.
Shared parking lot with a ramen shop and others (a few meters south of I' LULU CAFE)
There were signs for several shops on the sign at the entrance, and looking carefully, on a small ocher-based sign was the name "I' LULUCAFE" too 🤗

However, the time I went this time was right at lunchtime, and with space for about 5 cars, and it being a parking lot shared by several shops, it was completely full. (The ramen shop next door seems to be popular too.)
But after waiting a little, a space opened up, and I somehow managed to park.
I entered the shop and ordered the "Thai-style Okinawa soba". While waiting, I checked out the menu 😊

After a while, the "Thai-style Okinawa soba" came 😁
Thai-style Okinawa soba　¥900

There were various condiments next to the soba. The staff explained that they're lemon juice, sugar, chili and fish sauce, and to add them to taste. Thai cooking condiments, this is a new kind of Okinawa soba not found at other shops lol
First I wanted to taste the broth as is, so I took a sip without adding anything.
"?" It's completely different from the Okinawa soba broths I've had so far. A flavor I'd never tasted before.

I learned about this shop when I saw it featured in the newspaper, and when I checked the newspaper article I'd snapped a photo of, it said that rather than the standard bonito and pork stock used in the usual Okinawa soba broth, it seems to be the broth used in a dish called pho, a chicken stock. A new broth, different from the Okinawa soba I've had until now.
Thai-style Okinawa soba　¥900

Next I had the noodles. They're thick, straight, on-the-soft-side noodles. The topping is shibui (winter melon), soft and well soaked in flavor. Since shibui was also a topping at "Okinawa Soba Papaya to Subui" in Uruma City, which I introduced before, it reminded me of that.

The meat is chicken thigh rather than pork, and tender. There was cilantro in it too, and it was probably my first time eating it (;^ω^); I think it's an ingredient people either love or hate, but I didn't notice any particularly strong taste or aroma and ate it just fine lol　I have a dumb tongue lol

Partway through, I added the Thai condiments (lemon juice, fish sauce, chili) and enjoyed changing up the flavor. Maybe I added too little lemon juice and fish sauce, since I didn't feel much change. But the chili, maybe I put in too much, because from partway through I was eating with sweat pouring out (;^ω^)　Spicy.
Rating (9/15): A new kind of Okinawa soba. The Okinawa soba I know has turned into Thai food 😊　How about everyone trying this Okinawa soba at least once?

OKINAWA SOBA HITOTSU.name: OKINAWA SOBA HITOTSU
OKINAWA SOBA HITOTSU.desc: A stylish shop like a bar with exposed concrete. The signature is the Special Hitotsu Soba, with a blended broth of chicken, pork and bonito, topped with sea lettuce (āsa) and yushi-dofu (soft Okinawan tofu).
t: I ate here in October 2023. This shop was a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1–2024.2.29)", and I went as my 7th of 34 shops 😊
OKINAWA　SOBA　HITOTSU　Without the "Okinawa soba" banner flags, the stylish exterior doesn't look like an Okinawa soba shop at all 😊
There were other customers, so I couldn't take photos inside, but the exposed-concrete building had a stylish feel, somehow like a bar 😁
For my order, I decided on the "Special Hitotsu Soba" introduced in the stamp rally booklet 😊
Menu 1
Menu 2
Special Hitotsu Soba (medium) ¥900

The "Special Hitotsu Soba" came lol　First, the broth of course lol　After tasting the broth a few times with my spoon, I thought that within the blended stock of chicken, pork, bonito and so on, the pork bone was subtly winning out a little?

However, when I researched the shop after finishing eating, they had an Instagram, and on that Instagram it was described as "○Bonito broth on the other side of ○○ the chicken and pork soup○✨A soak-into-you style Okinawa soba✨" (;^ω^)

Maybe it's my dumb tongue, but I didn't feel the bonito was particularly strong. However, since the "Special Hitotsu Soba" has "yushi-dofu (soft Okinawan tofu)" as a topping, I also thought maybe its liquid combines with the broth so you get this kind of taste (;^ω^)　Sorry, I'm just guessing lol
Next I had the noodles 🙏 The noodles are a thin straight type, with a soft feel.
Special Hitotsu Soba (medium) ¥900

When I ate the sea lettuce (āsa) topping ("āsa" is what Okinawans call the seaweed "hitoegusa". It clings to rocks in the shallows along Okinawa's coast, and it's apparently in season and delicious from February to May. It's rich in dietary fiber, minerals and calcium, and especially packed with beta-carotene, so it seems to be effective for anti-aging and cancer prevention too. It apparently has about 8 times the calcium of milk and about 2 times the folic acid of spinach (according to info from Nakamura Soba)) tangled with the thin straight noodles, I could taste the aroma and flavor of the āsa 🤗
The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) were jiggly and tender, well soaked in flavor and delicious 😁
Rating (9/15): Plain tasty. The inside of the shop has a stylish atmosphere like a bar.
*The shop has no parking lot, so you'll have to park at a coin parking lot nearby.

When I sat down, the table guide said "Water is self-service" and "Please return your dishes to the return counter", a pleasant smartness like a cafe. There were also the business hours and an Instagram QR code, giving off a modern feel. Looking over the menu, besides Okinawa soba there were coffee, non-alcoholic drinks, craft beer, and the words "takeout available". On top of that there's "Nomakuro Oden" and "tebichi (pig's feet)" too, which got me a little excited. This time I ordered the "Nomakuro Soba (everything on top)", which shares the shop's name.
Nomakuro Soba (greedy all-toppings-on-top) ¥1,000

The bowl that arrived on a round tray first of all looks great in photos with its polka-dot pattern. The broth is a cloudy white pork bone stock type. Taking a sip, it's creamy. The savoriness of the bones spreads gently. It's on the rich track that reminds me of "Tsukikuruchi" in Uruma City, with depth too, and I felt it was carefully simmered.
Nomakuro Soba (greedy all-toppings-on-top) ¥1,000

The noodles are medium-thick and loosely curly. Lifted with chopsticks they shine glossily, and in your mouth they have a pleasant chewy spring that pushes back against your teeth. Thanks to the curls they coat themselves in broth, and when you slurp, the sweetness of the pork bone arrives softly at the same time. They're boiled on the slightly soft side, and combined with the creaminess of the broth, they create a "gentle sense of unity".

As the name says, the toppings are everything on top, and lively to look at too. The pig's feet (tebichi) are melt-in-your-mouth, and the jiggly bounce of the collagen is fun. The fat is well rendered, so you can eat it easily without feeling heavy. The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) are prepared lightly too, the gelatinous parts around the bone falling apart, and the more you chew the more the flavor seeps out. And what made me even happier was the white of the yushi-dofu (soft Okinawan tofu). Its silky softness that crumbles fluffily pairs perfectly with the milkiness of the broth, pulling the whole impression together into something much milder. The kelp and green onions add aromatic accents, and I also liked how the aftertaste doesn't get dull.

And on a small side plate, there was a little bit of freshly fried tempura. Two kinds, okra and chikuwa, with a thin batter that's light and crispy when you bite into it. Delicious 😋 Drinking a sip of broth, biting the tempura, then going back to the soba refreshes the flavor. The contrast in temperature is fun too, and it makes you feel like you got a little bonus. The contrast between the round tray and the small black plate looks great too 📷

The shop is new and clean, and the color scheme of the bright wood-grain tables with black spoons and dishes is stylish. Along the walls, carefully selected goods are lined up, with cups, fabric items and plants casually arranged, and I felt it would go over well with groups of women or on a date. There's a hand-drip coffee menu too, so it's nice that you can enjoy a cup after your meal.
Including the sense for presentation and tableware, the added value of the tempura, and the comfort of the shop, my satisfaction with the total experience is solidly high.
Rating (9/15): Next time it might be nice to also get the oden set or coffee and take my time. So, the taste lands at a calm "fairly tasty", but how about trying this shop at least once 🙂

This time I'm introducing a shop where you can have an especially rare experience, even among my Okinawa soba tours 😄 I learned about it in the newspaper: "yu-i FACTORY" in Arakawa, Haebaru Town. This shop is an ultra-rare Okinawa soba shop that's open only once a month, an Okinawa soba shop that uses that "habu" snake as a topping 😄
yu-i FACTORY

The moment I saw the exterior, it was such a unique building that I thought, "What kind of facility is this?" 😅 It has a stylish construction that looks like a renovated container house, and at first glance it's a modern atmosphere you'd never take for an Okinawa soba shop.

When you enter the shop, there's "habu soba" 😆 The ultimate oddball soba you can only taste in Okinawa. As someone who goes around eating Okinawa soba, this is something I absolutely have to take on 👍

What I ordered this time was the "Okinawa 82 Soba (Habu Soba) Set" for ¥1,300. I also ordered the limited-quantity ¥300 "Jushi with Habu Stock" along with it. A combination of Okinawan representatives ✖️3 — Okinawa soba, jushi and habu — there can't be a more Okinawan menu than this 😂
82 Soba (Habu Soba) Set　¥1,300

First, as usual, I taste the broth. It's quite a unique broth said to combine bonito, pork, chicken, kelp, and habu stock. Taking a sip… honestly, none of the stocks stood out, and if I hadn't been told it was habu I wouldn't have known 😅 But maybe that actually makes it easier to drink.
82 Soba (Habu Soba) Set　¥1,300
Next I have the noodles. They're a medium-thick straight type, with a soft-ish texture. My impression is that they're plain tasty Okinawa soba noodles 😊

And then the simmered habu, which you could call the star this time! When I timidly picked it up with my chopsticks, it had a ton of small bones and less meat than I expected 😅 There was no smell or quirkiness at all, and surprisingly it had a light flavor. But eating it while picking out the small bones was a bit of a struggle 💦
The rafute was simmered until tender, but it felt like a little sinewy texture remained. Even so, it was a reassuring flavor as a standard Okinawa soba topping 😄
82 Jushi　¥300 (limited quantity)

And I also taste the limited-quantity "Jushi with Habu Stock". This one was lightly seasoned too, and finished so that you wouldn't know it had habu stock in it unless you were told. But the unique lingering aftertaste left in my mouth after eating (earthy?) may perhaps be a characteristic of habu 🤔

Finishing my meal and looking around, a habu leather goods shop was also open in the prefab building next door 😆 The wallets combining indigo dye and habu leather were really cool, and appealing as a very Okinawan souvenir too ✨

Being open only once a month is a rare business style. Okinawa soba using habu, an ingredient unique to Okinawa, was a precious experience you absolutely can't have anywhere else 😊

To be honest, judging by taste alone it felt like ordinary Okinawa soba, but considering this rarity and the value of the experience, I think it's a shop worth trying at least once. It's definitely worth visiting by aiming for the once-a-month opening 👍

Rating (8.5/15): The taste itself is ordinary, but it's a shop where you can have a precious experience available only here, even within Okinawa, using the unusual ingredient habu. Including the rarity of opening only once a month, I think it's worth trying at least once if you love Okinawa soba 😄 However, while eating it didn't seem to have any quirkiness, after finishing there was something — not the gamy smell like after eating goat soba, but earthy? — a feeling different from usual, so be careful (^0^;)

From the menu, what I had this time was the manager's recommendation, the "Agariya Special". Just from the name, it has a special feel, right ✨
Agariya Special　¥1,250

The first thing that caught my attention was the broth's unique flavor. It's a blended stock of pork bone and bonito, but the pork bone comes forward gently, and it has more depth than I expected. You can taste the bonito flavor too, with the pork bone base gently working: that's the balance. It's a solid flavor, but the way it isn't too heavy is nice, and it feels ordinary 😊.
Agariya Special　¥1,250

The noodles are medium-thin, finished on the soft side. I think I prefer a bit more chewiness. But the pairing of soft noodles and this broth is surprisingly good, and the way it spreads softly in your mouth feels nice. And something you don't see much at other shops is the boiled egg. A boiled egg on Okinawa soba was a bit of a surprise, but it works as an accent in its own way, and I thought it was interesting.
Agariya Special　¥1,250 (a whole boiled egg is unusual 😆)

The seared soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), which you could call the star this time, give off the fragrant aroma of charcoal, and you can enjoy the aroma with every bite. The cartilage part is jiggly, soft and easy to eat. However, the meat part had a bit of a sinewy texture, and honestly I'd have liked it a bit more melt-in-your-mouth 😅. But people who like this level of searing will surely find it irresistible!
Wasabi and salt as condiments.

On top of that, the wasabi that came as a condiment was a slightly surprising accent. Wasabi on Okinawa soba…? I thought, but it goes surprisingly well! When you put a little dab of wasabi on the soki and eat it, the flavor changes to something refreshing, and it's delicious in its own way. It reminded me of "Ishigufu" and "Su~gi~ji", which has now moved to Onna Village and changed its name to "Sakihama Seimen". There was a nostalgic feeling, along with new discoveries, and it was a happy time 😌.

Overall, the Agariya Special at "Agariya+" is a well-balanced bowl throughout. But if you ask whether it has a standout point that makes it particularly special, maybe not really. Still, it's plenty for enjoying local Okinawa soba, and I felt it has a stability that makes you want to come back again and again. If I get the chance, I'd like to try other menu items too 🍜.

Rating (9/15): Everything is average and plain tasty. I have no complaints, but honestly I'd have liked a little more impact. This shop on the grounds of MaxValu has an unusual paid parking lot with no gate bar (cameras at the entrance/exit). The payment machine is on the shop side, so be careful. (You can get a free ticket from the shop, so parking is effectively free.)

"Ishigufu" is the shop of the "First Okinawa Soba King" and has branches in various areas. This time I ordered the "Ishigufu Special Selection Soba (with both bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki) and seared soki)".
Menu (this time I ordered the special selection soba)
Ishigufu Special Selection Soba (with bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki) and seared soki) ¥1,000
In the clear agu pork broth, the handmade noodles are smooth and firm and tasty 😄　The seared soki is melt-in-your-mouth, and the wasabi and mustard are an accent not found at other shops, nice 😄
Rating (9/15): "Kanucha Bay Resort" is also nearby, so how about it when you're staying there, driving along the east coast of northern Okinawa Island, or sightseeing?
PS: The handmade noodles are very firm, so depending on personal taste, some people may find them on the hard side.

いしぐふー（浦添大公園）.name: Ishigufu (Urasoe Daikoen)
いしぐふー（浦添大公園）.desc: The Urasoe Daikoen branch of Ishigufu, the "First Okinawa Soba King". A bowl with a light agu pork broth, chewy medium-thick noodles, and seared soki accented with wasabi and mustard.
t: "Ishigufu (Ishikufu)" is the shop of the "First Okinawa Soba King" and has branches in various areas. This time I ordered the "Seared Soki Soba" at the "Urasoe Daikoen branch" (March 2019).
Ishigufu (Urasoe Daikoen branch)
Seared Soki Soba　¥700

It seems that even under the same shop name, "Ishigufu" tastes a little different at each branch. Here it's a light agu pork broth with chewy, firm medium-thick noodles 😄 The seared soki is tender too, and the wasabi and mustard are an accent unique to Ishigufu, nice 😄
Rating (9/15): Plain tasty.
PS: Ishigufu's noodles are on the firm side, so some people may find them hard.

いちの屋.name: Ichinoya
いちの屋.desc: A shop in Isagawa, Nago City, along National Route 58. A broth with a strong bonito flavor, regular straight noodles and tender seared soki. There's also the big-volume specialty "Dekadeka Soba". Changing up the flavor with kōrēgūsu is recommended too.
t: It was introduced in the "Nago City Soba Map", and I ate here in October 2020 😄
Ichinoya (along National Route 58)
"Ichinoya" introduced as shop 36 of 41 in the "Nago Soba Map"

I ordered the "Seared Soki Soba". The bonito broth flavor is strong, and with the regular straight noodles, the seared soki was tender and tasty too 😋　Until then, I'd avoided kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori; an Okinawan seasoning of island chili peppers steeped in awamori) without ever trying it, but from around the time of this Ichinoya, I started to realize that adding it changes up the flavor of the broth so it's delicious twice over, and after that I began adding kōrēgūsu partway through 😄
Seared Soki Soba

Rating (9/15): I think it's plain tasty. In the soba map, a soba called "Dekadeka Soba" was described deliciously as "big volume with the aroma of pork bone and bonito stock", so if I get another chance I'd like to try it 😄　Also, I realized I'd been avoiding kōrēgūsu without trying it, and it changes up the flavor of the broth, so I recommend it, please give it a try.

いーばる家.name: Iibaru-ya
いーばる家.desc: A spacious shop marked by its roadside sign. A light broth with restrained pork bone and thin, slightly curly noodles. A community-rooted shop bustling with local customers.
t: *This article was created with the AI Claude 3.5 Sonnet, with some additions by me.
I ate here in June 2024 😄
This is Iibaru-ya's sign along the road.
Iibaru-ya
Inside the shop (it's quite spacious)
Inside the shop (near the entrance, someone's autograph is on display 😄)
I decided to order the "Soki Soba" from the meal ticket machine installed at the entrance.
Soki Soba (large)　¥900
Now, first, the broth. Taking a sip, you can tell the pork bone stock is working a little. However, it's restrained, and the impression is light.
Okinawa soba broth tends to show strong individuality from shop to shop, but "Iibaru-ya"'s broth falls into what you'd call the orthodox category.
There were no particularly standout features; it's an average finish as Okinawa soba broth, and I didn't find anything especially noteworthy. It feels plain tasty.
Soki Soba (large)　¥900
Next, the noodles. "Iibaru-ya"'s noodles are a thin, slightly curly straight type. They're boiled on the soft side.
The noodles are slightly on the thin side, but they cling to the broth well enough. However, if I state my personal preference, I felt they could have had a bit more firmness.
Finally, I'll touch on the toppings, especially the pork spare ribs (soki). Soki is one of the representative toppings of Okinawa soba, and the seasoning is the light type.
Also, it's a shame that the meat was a bit coarse and on the dry side.
I was also left dissatisfied with the volume of the soki. While the bones are quite large, the amount of meat is on the small side.
The other toppings (green onions, fish cake (kamaboko), etc.) were ordinary, with nothing especially noteworthy.

In summary, my overall impression of "Iibaru-ya"'s soki soba was "ordinary". It's not particularly bad, but it doesn't have features that leave a strong impression either. Certainly, when I visited it was bustling with local customers. There are many regulars too, and there's no doubt it's a popular shop rooted in the community. However, I didn't feel enough appeal to want to go out of my way to visit again.
Rating (9/15): It feels ordinary 😊　How about it for those who want to casually enjoy Okinawa soba when visiting Itoman City?

うかじそば.name: Ukaji Soba
うかじそば.desc: A shop convenient for sightseeing near Shuri Castle and Ryutan Pond. A light blended broth of pork, chicken and bonito, flat thin noodles, and melt-in-your-mouth soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki). A gentle bowl for those who like it light.
t: I ate here in February 2023 😄
Ukaji Soba (near Ryutan Pond)
Since it's close to tourist spots like Shuri Castle, I thought it might be crowded with tourists, but I was able to park in the lot in front of the shop, and it was empty.
Menu
Soft-bone Soki Soba (medium)　¥800

I ordered the Soft-bone Soki Soba (medium). The broth is the light type, a blended stock of pork, chicken and bonito. The noodles are flat and thin. The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) are melt-in-your-mouth and delicious, but the broth was too light, and it felt weak in flavor.
Rating (8.5/15): According to the explanation on the menu, they seem to be particular about the broth, but I'm sorry, to me the flavor was too weak, and I felt it was too light.

うちなーイタリアンSOLA.name: Uchina Italian SOLA
うちなーイタリアンSOLA.desc: An Italian restaurant near the Ganeko intersection on National Route 330. An oddball place that uses fresh Okinawa soba noodles even for its pasta. The specialty "Seared Meat Soba" is superb, with seared pork loin like thick-cut ham and smooth, chewy homemade noodles. *There is information that they stopped serving Okinawa soba around May 2024.
t: *As of May 2024, there is information that they no longer serve Okinawa soba on the lunch menu, so please be careful. It was honestly one of the Okinawa sobas I thought was delicious, so it's a shame (;｡;)

Uchina Italian SOLA. Along National Route 330, near the Ganeko intersection

Wow lol　I'd often seen this shop while driving on the national highway, but I'd never seen an Okinawa soba banner standing like this at lunchtime, and from the shop name I'd never thought it was an Okinawa soba shop (;^ω^)　I'd thought it was just an ordinary Italian restaurant (;^ω^)
The business hours seem relatively short, 12:00 to 14:30, so maybe that's why I'd never seen the Okinawa soba banner flag lol
The entrance on the 2nd floor. It has an Italian feel 😊

The menu at the entrance. They have a full lineup of authentic Okinawa soba dishes (;^ω^)　Since it's an Italian restaurant, they have pasta and pizza too. But looking carefully, the pasta seems to use Okinawa soba noodles. Maybe that's why the shop name is "Uchina Italian"?
The menu at the entrance
The menu at the entrance
Inside the shop. It has an Italian feel lol
Entering the shop, it did indeed have an Italian feel, as in the photo above 😁　On top of that, I don't know if it's for the pasta or pizza, but there was a nice smell of cheese in the shop 🤗
The stamp rally booklet
The "Seared Meat Soba" was introduced in the stamp rally booklet, so I ordered it.
Menu 1

There seem to be 2 kinds of noodles, and you choose from "eggless noodles" or "egg noodles". When I asked the staff for their recommendation, they said "egg noodles", so I chose those. Also, the Seared Meat Soba was relatively reasonable at ¥850 even for a large, so I ordered a large 😁　Among the stamp rally shops I'd eaten at so far, my impression was that many were in the ¥1,000-or-so price range, so I thought ¥850 for a large at this shop was reasonable.
Menu 2. The pasta seems to use Okinawa soba noodles. These Italian dishes look delicious too 😊
Menu 3. Italian chilled soba using Okinawa soba noodles. This one looks plain tasty too 😋
Seared Meat Soba (large) ¥850
While I was playing around looking at the menu, the Seared Meat Soba came lol　The meat somehow has a look not found at other shops.

Next, I'll have the noodles 😋
Seared Meat Soba (large) ¥850
As written on the menu, they're thick-ish straight noodles. The smooth, chewy homemade fresh noodles are delicious too 😋
Next, I'll have the meat. This topping is different from other shops; it seems to be seared pork loin, but it's like thick-cut ham, and this too feels fresh and is delicious 😋.

Rating (12/15): I thought the toppings, noodles and broth were all high-level. The smooth, chewy homemade fresh noodles and the seared pork loin like thick-cut ham are especially delicious. The inside of the shop has an Italian feel and a nice atmosphere. I'd really like you to try it once, I recommend it.

うっちや～.name: Utchiya~
うっちや～.desc: A precious shop on the Motobu Peninsula where you can eat morning soba from 7 a.m. A rich bonito broth with chewy, medium-thick, flat fresh noodles. There's also a fun custom of ringing a bell on your way out.
t: *This article was created by AI (Claude Haiku 4.5), with parts added to and updated by me 😆
I went to eat here in January 2025 😁😊
This time I visited "Utchiya~" in Nakaoshi, Nakijin Village. This shop actually opens from 7 a.m., so a big feature is that you can eat morning soba.
Utchiya~

Shops in the Motobu Peninsula area where you can enjoy Okinawa soba from the morning are surprisingly rare. The exterior is a cute, very Okinawan building based on white, marked by a wooden noren (shop curtain). I visited just past noon, and there was a good mix of local customers and tourists, with a lively atmosphere in the air.
Meal ticket machine
They do morning soba too 😆
Inside the shop
Inside the shop

The interior is a traditional Okinawan construction using lots of wood, with counter seats and tatami seating too, a well-prepared environment for enjoying Okinawa soba calmly. It's an ordering system using the ticket machine, so it keeps the atmosphere of a local shop while letting you order smoothly, which left a good impression ✨　What I had this time was the "Utchiya~ Soba".
Utchiya~ Soba (large)　¥980

When I'm actually in front of the bowl, the aroma of the broth with its bonito stock spreads pleasantly. You can taste the saltiness properly too; it's by no means bland, but rather has a moderate richness. It's finished as a well-balanced, delicious broth 🎯
Utchiya~ Soba (large)　¥980
Apparently they use carefully made fresh noodles

The noodles are carefully made fresh noodles, with a distinctive shape that's medium-thick and flat. The chewy texture is pleasant, and they cling to the broth outstandingly. There's solid chewiness left too, and rather than smooth, the unique springy texture is what leaves an impression. The texture of these noodles certainly has a personality different from other shops, and it feels nice 👍

Looking at the toppings, there are soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), a soft-boiled egg, green onions, and a small amount of sea lettuce (āsa) (seaweed). The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) are well soaked with a soy-sauce-based flavor, and you can taste sweetness too. However, a fair amount of sinewy texture remains, so while they're satisfying to eat, the slightly fibrous parts are a bit noticeable. The soft-boiled egg is a style you don't see much at other shops, and the small amount of sea lettuce (āsa) is also a nice, very Okinawa-soba-like touch.

The fact that many local customers visit speaks to the high quality of this shop. There are a fair number of tourists too, and there's a nice atmosphere with a good balance of locals and tourists. And what's interesting is that there's a custom of ringing the bell in the shop when you leave, to convey that "it was delicious" 😅
It seems you ring the bell when you leave the shop? lol

This is an unusual touch, and I think it's a lovely system for expressing your satisfaction after eating. Above all, being open from 7 a.m. is a big point. For people who want to be active from early morning on their trip, being able to eat morning soba loved by local customers is an advantage not found at other shops. If you build it into your sightseeing route in the Motobu Peninsula area, you'll have an even more fulfilling Okinawa soba tour.

Rating (10/15): I thought it's a shop that lets you taste top-level deliciousness for the Motobu Peninsula area. With the unusual feature of serving morning soba too, I felt it's a shop worth visiting at least once. Those who want to immerse themselves in the charm of Okinawa soba from the morning, please do pay it a visit 🍜

うみちか食堂.desc: A local diner in Mashiki, Ginowan City. Reasonably priced, like the Umichika Soba with gentle bonito broth (medium ¥700), with unique menu items such as squid ink soba and bean sprout and garlic chive stir-fry soba. Finishing with zenzai is recommended too.

Umichika Shokudo

Umichika Suba (medium)　¥700

うむさんの庭.name: Umusan no Niwa

The specialty "Charcoal-Seared Thick-Cut Braised Pork Belly Soba" features braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) so tender you can cut it with chopsticks and so fragrant it's No.1 class among all toppings I've had. The lemon-water hospitality is stylish too.

The sign along National Route 58 (turn right at this sign)

Menu (the touch panel system is nice)
Menu (the touch panel system is nice)

It's a stylish, creative menu of Okinawa soba. All of them look delicious, but I figured the item shown at the very top was probably the recommendation, so I decided to order the "Charcoal-Seared Thick-Cut Braised Pork Belly Soba".
Inside the shop (there were other customers, so sorry, I couldn't photograph the left side, but the shop is spacious)

Lemon in the pitcher. Refreshing lemon water, delicious
Charcoal-Seared Thick-Cut Braised Pork Belly Soba　¥1,200

Charcoal-Seared Thick-Cut Braised Pork Belly Soba　¥1,200

It's a big piece of braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), but when I lift it with my chopsticks, it breaks apart (°°)　It's very tender 😁　And since it's seared over charcoal, it's fragrant and very tasty 😋
I thought it was the most delicious braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) of all the Okinawa soba shops I've eaten at so far. I recommend it.

Rating (12/15): This shop is in a sightseeing spot in Onna Village. The charcoal-seared thick-cut braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) is superb. I thought it was the best of all the Okinawa soba toppings I've eaten so far (as of February 2024). Even the water is lemon water, stylish in a way not found at other shops, so how about trying it once? I recommend it 😄

うるくそば.name: Uruku Soba
うるくそば.desc: The TOMITON branch, inside the "Okinawa Soba Expo" food court at Toyosaki's TOMITON. Its feature is that you can choose the broth from pork bone or bonito, and the No.1 most popular dish is the sweet-savory soft-bone soki soba. A casual bowl while you're out shopping.

Uruku Soba TOMITON branch

At the shop front, food samples and menus are lined up in a row, and besides Okinawa soba, the menu is quite extensive with set meals, curry, taco rice and more ✨ Families can each order what they like, so my impression was that it seems easy to use.
Looking at the showcase, the one introduced as "Popularity Ranking No.1" was the soft-bone soki soba. Since I was there anyway, this time I tried ordering the popular dish!
This shop's feature is that you can choose the broth from pork bone flavor or bonito flavor. This time, since I like bonito broth, I chose the bonito flavor without hesitation 😊
Soft-bone Soki Soba (bonito broth)　¥700

The soft-bone soki soba that was brought out is a simple bowl with two large soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) on a clear broth. Starting with the broth, the bonito stock comes through more strongly than I expected. The moment it hits your mouth the bonito aroma spreads, and while it's light, I could fully feel the presence of the stock.
Soft-bone Soki Soba (bonito broth)　¥700

The noodles are medium-thick curly noodles. They're boiled on the soft side, with an old-fashioned Okinawa-soba-like texture. Rather than the type where you enjoy firmness, my impression was of gentle noodles you can slurp down smoothly together with the broth.

And the star, the soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), are well soaked with a sweet seasoning. Overall, it was a well-balanced bowl and plain tasty 😊
However, my honest impression is, "It's tasty, but I think there are other Okinawa soba shops that would move me more~" 😂

Rating (9/15): Plain tasty. The shop is easy to walk into, and being inside a shopping mall, the ease of using it casually is a big draw. I felt it's just the right shop for when you "want to have a quick Okinawa soba" on your way home from shopping or in the middle of sightseeing ✨

おかあさん.name: Okaasan

I ate here in September 2024 😄

Okaasan
"Okaasan" is characterized by a simple exterior marked by its red sign. Entering the shop, a warm atmosphere spreads out 😌

Soft-bone Soki Soba　¥900

After a while, the long-awaited "Soft-bone Soki Soba" makes its appearance! 🍜 First, let's taste the broth. The gentle pork-bone-based broth has a flavor that somehow feels nostalgic. It feels plain tasty.
Soft-bone Soki Soba　¥900

And then the main topping, the soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki). The soy sauce flavor is on the strong side, and a slightly sweet seasoning is characteristic. They're simmered until melt-in-your-mouth, but a little sinewy texture remains.

However, if I give my personal impression, the taste struck me as ordinary. It wasn't surprisingly delicious, but there's no doubt it delivers stable deliciousness.
When you visit Itoman City, why not try the Okinawa soba at "Okaasan", loved by locals, at least once? 😉 You're sure to enjoy the simple flavor and warm atmosphere!

Rating (9/15): It feels ordinary 😊　Overall, "Okaasan" delivers stable deliciousness. It's not a surprising taste, but it was a simple, warm Okinawa soba that lets you understand why it continues to be loved by locals. Everyone, please do pay it a visit! 🚶‍♂️🏃‍♀️

おきなわすばやぁ太陽.name: Okinawa Subayaa Taiyo
おきなわすばやぁ太陽.desc: An Okinawa soba shop in the food court of Uruma City's farmers' market facility "Uru Marche". It's fun that you can choose your noodles, such as curly noodles, fresh sea lettuce (āsa) noodles and fresh mozuku noodles, and they also have goat soba and nationwide shipping. You can casually enjoy a bowl at the open outdoor seats.
t: *This article was created with AI (ChatGPT 4o) and partly added to by me 😆
I ate here in October 2024 😄
This time I visited "Okinawa Subayaa Taiyo" in the food court of "Uru Marche" in Uruma City!
Okinawa Subayaa Taiyo (inside the Uru Marche food court)
🌺Various shops are lined up in the food court, and they all look delicious, so it's hard to decide 😋.
There are all kinds of shops inside the Uru Marche food court

What I chose from among them was, of course, the "Soft-bone Soki Soba" at Okinawa soba stamp rally participant "Okinawa Subayaa Taiyo". Normally I always order the Okinawa soba introduced in the stamp rally booklet, but for this shop it was "goat soba" that was introduced, and after eating goat soba before at "Mukashi Mukashi" in Nago City, the impression of the gamy smell afterward stayed with me strongly, so somehow I couldn't choose it (^0^;)　I gave up on it this time (^0^;)　While I was eating it, I thought it had no quirkiness (^0^;)　It's the after-meal part that bothers me 😄
They also ship Okinawa suba nationwide 😄
It's nice that you can choose the noodles too 👍
Menu panel board
There's also goat (hijaa) soba.
On top of that, for the noodles I tried choosing "fresh mozuku noodles" 🎶. I'm looking forward to the unusual noodle texture!

While waiting for the soba at the roofed outdoor seats, a pleasant breeze blew in and I was in the best mood ☀️. Eating in an open space like this on a nice day feels really good, doesn't it. It really boosts the vacation mood too ⛱️.
It feels nice outdoors 😄
It feels nice outdoors 😄

And now, the long-awaited soba arrives ✨. The bowl is full of jiggly soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki)! The broth has a clear color, and the fresh mozuku noodles look delicious too 🍜. My heart is full of anticipation: time to eat!
Soft-bone Soki Soba　¥800

First, a sip of the broth. The pork-bone-based stock comes through solidly, with a deep flavor 😊. However, overall the saltiness is a bit on the strong side, so opinions may be divided. But it might be perfect for people who like strong flavors!
Soft-bone Soki Soba　¥800

Next I have the "fresh mozuku noodles". They have a chewy, springy texture that's satisfying to eat ✨! However, to be honest, the "mozuku feel" is a bit restrained, and the flavor is on the faint side? 🤔　That said, there's mozuku in it as a topping, so eating them together, you can properly enjoy the mozuku. The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) 🍖 are tender and melt-in-your-mouth too 😳

Rating (9/15): My overall impression is "fairly plain tasty", but with the openness of eating outdoors and the liveliness of the whole food court added in, I had a fun time 😊. Also, Uru Marche has lots of other gourmet food too, so next time I'd like to try other shops as well 🍔🍣.
"Okinawa Subayaa Taiyo" was a shop you can drop into casually and enjoy Okinawa soba in a relaxed way 🍜. When you head out to Uru Marche, please do pay it a visit! 🌈

お肉の店仲村.name: Oniku no Mise Nakamura
お肉の店仲村.desc: An Okinawa soba shop run by a pork specialty store. It uses Terukina Soba's handmade noodles, and the Special Soba topped with spare-rib-style soki, pig's feet (tebichi) and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) has big impact. Carefully selected pork and beef are also sold at the shop front.
t: I ate here in December 2023. This shop was a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1–2024.2.29)", and I went as my 25th of 34 shops 😊
Oniku no Mise Nakamura ("Meat Shop Nakamura")　*From the shop name alone, you can't tell it's an Okinawa soba shop (^0^;)
With this shop, it's hard to realize it's an Okinawa soba shop from the name alone (^0^;) But looking carefully, the cute pig on the sign is promoting Okinawa soba (lol)
*You can park about 4 cars in the parking lot out back.
Menu

I went straight into the shop and checked the menu. First there's an explanation of the noodles. It says, "We use Terukina Soba's handmade noodles." On top of that, these noodles "can't be bought at the supermarket", which gave me a sense of anticipation that they'd be delicious 😄
Menu
This time I decided to order the "Special Soba (medium)" introduced in the stamp rally booklet.
Menu
Being a pork specialty store, they have a lineup of rice bowls too 😁　In the photo of the bone soup, the toppings are out of control (^0^;)
Menu
True to a meat specialty store, they sell meat too lol　They handle not only pork but beef too 😆
Menu
Apparently carefully selected pork is butchered at this shop. I'm looking forward to the meat too 😄
Special Soba (medium)　¥900

It came 😁　The toppings have impact; as expected of a pork specialty store, there's soki like spare ribs, and pig's feet (tebichi) (pork trotters), which I haven't had in a while lol　Also thinly sliced braised pork belly (sanmai-niku).
But first, as usual, the broth. Thinking "Hm?", I tasted the broth several times with my spoon. It looks rich in color, but it's a quite light seasoning with a faint pork-bone-based stock.
Next, the braised pork belly (sanmai-niku). This too has a surprisingly light seasoning, and it feels like a little sinewy texture remains.
Special Soba (medium)　¥900

Next, I have the "Terukina Soba handmade noodles". These noodles are medium-thick and a straight type. On the soft side. Continuing with the toppings, the pig's feet (tebichi). These are tender and full of collagen, but the seasoning feels weak. The spare-rib-style soki also has tender meat, but the flavor feels light.
Fuchiba (mugwort for free topping)

It wasn't placed on the table where I sat, but on the next table there was fuchiba (mugwort). In the second half I ate just a little with the noodles, and the faint bitterness makes a nice accent. I wish it had been placed on my table too.

Rating (8/15): Well, hearing it was Okinawa soba from a pork specialty store, I got my hopes up, but the broth felt weak in flavor, and while the meat had visual impact, I ended up thinking other shops' meat is just plain tastier.

がじまるそば.name: Gajimaru Soba
がじまるそば.desc: A soba shop operating at lunchtime that's the izakaya "iZAKAYA" at night. The signature is the Gajimaru Soba with a blended pork bone × bonito broth and lots of green onions, plus reasonable menu items like the ¥500 Nikuzu Soba. Look for the kijimuna sign.
t: This time I visited "Gajimaru Soba" in Gusukuma, Urasoe City. I went to eat here in March 2025 😁😊
Gajimaru Soba

Looking at the exterior, the big sign on the building's wall reading "iZAKAYA　Sake, Snacks and Charcoal Grill　Gajimaru Soba" catches the eye 😄　The sign has illustrations of a banyan tree and a kijimuna, giving off a very Okinawan atmosphere.
Gajimaru Soba
Gajimaru Soba

Near the entrance there's a yellow, handwritten-style guide sign reading "Gajimaru Soba →" and a stand with menu photos, so even first-timers can get there without getting lost ✨　Lanterns hang at the entrance, giving a glimpse of its other face as an izakaya at night.
Inside the shop

Stepping into the shop, a simple yet stylish space opens up, with counter seats lined along walls in an exposed-concrete style. There's a big TV mounted on the wall, so it feels like you can eat leisurely while watching TV 😊　It's cash only, so don't forget to have cash ready (these days more and more shops accept cashless payment, so I do hope something can be done about this lol).
Menu
Menu

Looking at the menu, starting with the signature "Gajimaru Soba (¥980)", there's a richly varied lineup with "Nikuzu Soba (¥500)", "Meat-Piled Mazesoba (¥880)", "Braised Pork Belly Soba (¥700)" and "Vegetable Soba (¥700)". What stands out is that the "Nikuzu Soba" is set at quite a reasonable ¥500 🎵　On top of that, side dishes like "Small Soba ¥300", "Pork Tamago Onigiri ¥200" and "Curry Rice ¥400" are plentiful too, so it seems they'd make good companions for the evening izakaya hours as well. By the way, looking at the drink menu, they have everything from awamori, shochu, highballs and chuhai to jasmine (matsurika) cocktails, and apparently there's an all-you-can-drink plan for ¥2,000. If you came at night, the drinks would surely be delicious lol 🍺
The ice water looks like a chuhai (^0^;)
This time I ordered the "Gajimaru Soba (¥980)", which shares the shop's name. If you're going to eat here, you've got to try the soba bearing the shop's name 😊

While I was waiting at the table, the Gajimaru Soba appeared on a wooden tray, set on the table's glossy, stylish top 🍜　The visual of a very Okinawan bowl with a pale blue rim topped with plenty of green onions whets the appetite.
Gajimaru Soba　¥980

First, as usual, a sip of the broth. It's a blended stock of pork bone and bonito, finished so you can properly taste the savoriness of both 😋　If anything, the pork bone comes through slightly more. It feels plain tasty.
Gajimaru Soba　¥980
Next, lifting the noodles, medium-thick curly noodles appeared 😄　You can clearly see the wavy curls. Eating them, they have a slightly chewy texture.

For toppings there are both braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), with a chunky sense of volume ✨　However, both the braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and the soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) had quite a sinewy texture, and honestly I'd have been even happier if they'd been simmered a bit more melt-in-your-mouth 😅　The green onion topping is generous, and its crisp texture and refreshing aroma make a nice accent
Rating (9/15): All in all, it was a stable bowl that's "plain tasty"~. It's the lunchtime operation of a shop that's an izakaya at night, so when you're in the area, why not drop by?

きしもと食堂八重岳店.name: Kishimoto Shokudo Yaedake branch
きしもと食堂八重岳店.desc: The Yaedake branch of the long-established "Kishimoto Shokudo", founded in Meiji 38 (1905). The menu has a clean-cut single item: "Kishimoto Soba" with wood-ash noodles. A solid flavor with authentic bonito broth; a line is a given, but turnover is fast.
t: It's a shop whose name often comes up when you search "Okinawa soba", so I went in March 2023 😀　This was my first time at an Okinawa soba shop in Motobu Town 😁
Kishimoto Shokudo (Yaedake branch)　I lined up a little, but turnover was fast and the wait was short
The menu is just one item: "Kishimoto Soba (extra-large) (large) (small)". Somehow that's cool.
The menu is only one item, Kishimoto Soba (it's a style where you choose the size and buy a meal ticket)
I ordered "Kishimoto Soba (large)" from the meal ticket machine.
Kishimoto Soba (large)　¥850
First, a sip of the broth. An authentic bonito broth with a solid flavor. It's delicious, but it felt a bit salty. I drank it all to the end, but I thought some people might find it salty.

The noodles are Okinawa soba made using wood ash, a slightly thick medium-thick type. They go well with the broth 😀　The toppings are green onions, fish cake (kamaboko), and lean pork and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), well seasoned, tender and delicious.
Rating (9.5/15): I thought the broth was a bit salty, but the noodles, broth and toppings were all well balanced and delicious overall.

きんそば.name: Kin Soba
きんそば.desc: A shop with real skill, with an aromatic broth blending kelp and chicken bones into a bonito-forward stock. You can choose from 3 kinds of noodles from Nishizaki Seimenjo, and the yushi-dofu (soft Okinawan tofu) from Unashi Tofu-ten is superb too. A bowl I think is the best in the Shuri area.
t: I ate here in December 2023. This shop was a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1–2024.2.29)", and I went as my 29th of 34 shops 😊
Kin Soba
Kin Soba entrance
This shop opens at 11:00, so I came timed to the opening, and wow, the 3 parking spaces in front of the shop filled up all at once (^0^;)
I thought, this is a popular shop 😄
Inside the shop

This shop is pay-first, and you pay at the counter. As the stamp rally booklet introduction said, "A broth blending kelp and chicken bones into a bonito-forward stock!", there's a nice bonito-based smell in the shop 🤤　The broth seems delicious from the smell alone.
This time I ordered the "Kin Soba" introduced in the stamp rally booklet. On top of that, they accept cashless payment (PayPay), and being able to pay quickly is nice too 😆
Menu
Explanation of their dedication to noodles

At this "Kin Soba", you choose from 3 kinds of noodles from Nishizaki Seimenjo. When I asked the staff for a recommendation, they answered that "No.1 (fresh noodles) and No.2 (whole wheat fresh noodles) are ordered a lot", so I figured No.1 must be the recommendation after all and chose "fresh noodles" lol
Kin Soba　¥880

From the stamp rally booklet introduction and the delicious smell of bonito broth wafting through the shop, I already knew it was bonito broth as I took a sip of the broth. No doubt about it, a delicious broth where the bonito stock really comes through 😋
Kin Soba　¥880
Next, I have the fresh noodles. The translucent noodles are medium-thick with a chewy texture. These are delicious too. The texture is fairly thick, like udon, and satisfying to eat 😄
Next, the topping of yushi-dofu (soft Okinawan tofu) from Unashi Tofu-ten. You can taste the flavor of the tofu, and this is tasty too. It seemed to me like tofu that had just been freshly made.
However, what was disappointing among the toppings was the meat (^0^;)　The braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) had a sinewy texture remaining, and I thought it was just one step short.

Rating (10.5/15): I felt the bonito-forward broth, the chewy fresh noodles and the yushi-dofu (soft Okinawan tofu) were very delicious. What's disappointing is that the meat has a sinewy texture, which is a shame. There were several autographs in the shop too, and I thought it's a popular shop, but the parking seems limited, so right after opening may be the way to go.
I think it's the most delicious of the Okinawa soba shops in Naha's Shuri area that I've eaten at so far, so how about everyone trying it once?

くくる.name: Kukuru
くくる.desc: A shop of "Rich Tantan Okinawa Soba" along Prefectural Route 7. A spicy broth fragrant with sesame, with homemade noodles aged for 48 hours with seafood powder mixed in. Free large noodles plus an after-meal ice cream. The solid homemade chili paste kōrēgūsu is unusual too.
t: I ate here in October 2023. This shop was a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1–2024.2.29)", and I went as my 2nd of 34 shops 😊
"Kukuru" along Prefectural Route 7

I'd often seen this shop on my way back from the point where I always surf (Itoman City: Suicide Cliff point), and I'd always wanted to eat here someday, and when I learned it was a participant in the "Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally" that I'd found out about a few days earlier, I was finally pushed to go in (;^ω^)

There are Okinawa soba shops all over that I've never been to, so it's hard to decide (;^ω^)　But this time I had a goal of prioritizing the 34 shops participating in the limited-time stamp rally, so I went in lol
The stamp rally booklet has an introduction to each shop and a photo of what seems to be their recommended Okinawa soba, so I decided to order that.
For "Kukuru" this time, "Rich Tantan Okinawa Soba" was introduced, so I ordered that. It was featured at the very top of the meal ticket machine too, so it seems to be this shop's top pick 🤗
The meal ticket machine installed near the entrance　The upper-left button is the "Rich Tantan Okinawa Soba" shown in the photo above.
Rich Tantan Okinawa Soba　¥930　Large noodles (free)

First, as usual, the broth 😁　It's completely different from the bonito-stock, pork-stock and chicken-stock types of Okinawa soba I usually eat lol　It's not super spicy, but it's a little spicy, and you can taste the sesame aroma and flavor too. It feels like ordinary tantanmen 😊　The noodles seem to have seafood powder in them, and you can tell something is kneaded into them. The aged noodles, rested for 48 hours, have a chewy texture and are delicious.
Vinegar and Sichuan pepper flowers were brought out with the Rich Tantan Okinawa Soba, so I added those in the second half.

I thought I'd added quite a lot of vinegar, but since the broth is rich to begin with, I couldn't really tell the change in flavor (;^ω^)　You may not be able to experience the flavor change unless you add a lot.
Menu placed on the table　Next time I'd like to try the regular Okinawa soba too
Anyway, I got my stamp for shop 2 of 34 😁

Kōrēgūsu (homemade chili paste) promoted above the meal ticket machine　Usually it's a liquid, but this kōrēgūsu is solid, which is unusual. It didn't come with the Rich Tantan Okinawa Soba, but I'd like to try it someday too.

Rating (9.5/15): It was more tantanmen than Okinawa soba 😊　The carefully made homemade noodles had a chewy texture and were delicious. For those who want to eat something different from regular Okinawa soba, how about this Rich Tantan Okinawa Soba? It comes with large noodles and an after-meal ice cream (brown sugar OR mango) sweet too.

くわっちぃやー食堂.name: Kwacchiiya Shokudo
くわっちぃやー食堂.desc: A community-rooted diner in Asato, Nakagusuku Village. A soupy soki soba with a bonito broth that comes through, and it's nice that it comes with complimentary jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice). A shop lined with autograph boards, like the center of local lunchtime.
t: *This article was created with AI (ChatGPT 5.2 Thinking) and partly added to by me 😆　I ate here in February 2025 😄

I went on an Okinawa soba tour in Asato, Nakagusuku Village 🍜✨　This time I visited "Kwacchiiya Shokudo". At a glance, the location is along the street with a simple exterior that makes you go "Oh, is this it?", and the sign has a lot of character too.
Kwacchiiya Shokudo

Location-wise it's not the kind of place packed with tourists, and honestly I went in thinking "Maybe it's quiet today?", but it was surprisingly bustling with local customers. I think this kind of "diner that's part of everyday life" feel is one of the good things about Okinawa soba~ 😊
Meal ticket machine near the entrance inside the shop
Menu posted inside the shop

When you enter it's a meal ticket style, with a big ticket machine. The menu is easy to understand too, and my impression is that Okinawa soba, soki soba and tebichi soba and the like are solidly covered. This time I went with "Soki Soba" without hesitation. And happily, it comes with complimentary jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice)… that gets me excited 🍚✨
Autographs of famous people posted inside the shop

While waiting, I looked around the shop and there were autograph boards all in a row, giving off an air that this must be a shop that's been loved for a long time~. The interior isn't flashy either, with a calming feel; there are people who eat quickly and leave, and people eating while leisurely chatting, and it felt like the center of local lunchtime.
Soki Soba (regular)　¥950 (jushi free)

Now, here's the soki soba that arrived. My first impression is "soupy!" There's a generous amount of broth, and from the look alone it's the "warm-you-up type". Taking a sip, the bonito broth comes through. Honestly, it's not the "super shocking!" type, but it has a reassuring feel where you can honestly say it's "fairly tasty" ☺️
Soki Soba (regular)　¥950 (jushi free)

The noodles are a medium-thick straight type, with a soft-ish texture. Rather than hitting you with firmness, they're the smooth, easy-to-eat type. I think people who like soft noodles will get hooked, and conversely people in the "plump and firm camp" may find them a little lacking. The memorable punch is restrained… that's where it stands.

And then the star, the bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki). They look like they have solid presence, but the seasoning is the light type. While there are tender parts, there are also parts where a bit of sinewy texture remains.

I also have the complimentary jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice). This too is lightly flavored, not the richly cooked type, a just-right balance when eaten with the soba. Since the soki soba is soupy, eating it alternately with the jushi feels like it resets your mouth, and this was a welcome combination 🍚🍜

Rating (9/15): My honest take overall is that rather than "I totally recommend it!", it's "an ordinary bowl that makes you want to keep coming as a local". It's not flashy, but there's the soupy broth with bonito stock coming through, the soft-ish medium-thick straight noodles, the light soki, and the complimentary jushi. With this set, there's solid satisfaction. Rather than making it a sightseeing destination where you "absolutely must go", my impression was that it's a shop to drop into casually when you're nearby and enjoy everyday Okinawa soba 🏝️✨　It makes sense that it's bustling with local customers.

けんぱーのすばやー.name: Kenpa no Subaya
けんぱーのすばやー.desc: A popular shop near Naha Shintoshin Park. Its feature is the clear golden (kugani) broth finished over 2 days with a golden ratio of pork, bonito and salt. There are autographs from Norika Fujiwara and Yoko Gushiken too. The serving speed feels great as well.
t: ― 2nd visit (August 2023) ―
I went to eat here in August 2023 😊　This is about a year after the previous time 😁

I actually wanted to go to an Okinawa soba shop I'd never eaten at, and I was driving from the north toward the south looking for one, but in the end the time for an errand was approaching, so I decided to go into this one, which was plain tasty when I ate it last time lol
Kenpa no Subaya (near Naha Shintoshin Park)

It was lunchtime and bustling with local customers and tourists, and I didn't have much time, so for a moment I thought, "Will this take quite a while? Should I leave?", but thinking "I might just make it?", I ordered the "Nankotsu Suba (regular size)" at the meal ticket machine.
After that, I secured a counter seat along the wall.

When I ate here last time I didn't really notice (my powers of observation are way too lacking (^_^;)), but I realized the walls are plastered with tons of autographs from celebrities and famous people from Okinawa Prefecture (^_^;)
The autographs posted at the wall-side counter where I happened to sit
Looking at the autographs one by one, what suddenly caught my eye, although the autograph is from a while back, was none other than Norika Fujiwara's autograph 😊

*I only noticed while writing this blog now, but the autograph posted below Norika Fujiwara's was from Yoko Gushiken, the former world boxing champion I respect, a star of the people of Okinawa Prefecture known by the nickname "Kanmuri Washi (Crested Serpent Eagle)" (^_^;)
Norika Fujiwara's autograph (sorry, I only noticed while writing the blog, so I didn't take a photo of Yoko Gushiken's autograph posted below it and can't show it lol)

Several people had ordered before me, so I'd braced myself that it would take a fair amount of time, but in about the time it took to gaze at the autographs on the wall for a bit, the "Nankotsu Suba (regular size)" I ordered came out.
This sense of speed, where you order quickly and it comes out quickly, is great ✌　My rating went up 😁
This is about other shops, but in the past I've experienced Okinawa soba shops that took quite a long time after ordering, even though they were popular shops, so I got a very good impression 😊
Nankotsu Suba (regular size)　¥850
As expected, this clear broth of "Kenpa no Subaya" is distinctive and nice 😊

Like last time, this clear broth and the thin noodles feel so "Kenpa no Subaya", nice. First, a sip of the standard broth; as always, there's no doubt it's a delicious broth with the bonito stock coming through 😊
The noodles are plain tasty too. After savoring the plain bonito-stock broth, I added Kenpa's kōrēgūsu (chili-infused awamori) that was on the table to change up the flavor.

This is plain tasty too 😋　Next, the soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) topping. They're tender and plain tasty in flavor, but not super melt-in-your-mouth, and there were sinewy soft-bone ribs in there too, so they had chewiness, and the sinewy meat got stuck between my teeth, so I needed a toothpick's help too (^_^;)

Rating (10/15): Plain tasty 😊　As expected, with the recent rise in prices, it seems the price has gone up compared to a year ago. The soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) felt a bit sinewy, and I needed a toothpick to get the meat stuck in my teeth lol　I think it's plain tasty, so how about it when you come to Naha Shintoshin for sightseeing and such?
― 1st visit (May 2022) ―
I went to eat here in May 2022 😊

On the official website it says: [The concept of our soba making is "harmony". To bring out a harmonious flavor, we repeated failure over and over again, yet without giving up and without compromise, we finally arrived at the unshakable golden ratio of pork, bonito and salt.

The golden (kugani) broth, finished over 2 days, has depth within its clarity; with the faintly fragrant bonito flavor and an exquisite level of salt, it is a bowl of soul made by summoning every ounce of our strength.]
They're really particular about the broth 😊
Kenpa no Subaya (near Naha Shintoshin Park)
I ordered the "Seared Nankotsu Green Onion Suba".
Menu
Seared Nankotsu Green Onion Suba　¥800

The clear, transparent broth that you don't see much at other shops has the gentle taste of bonito stock. After drinking about half the broth, I enjoy changing up the flavor with homemade chili oil 😊　The flavor change is a nice accent lol　The noodles are also ramen-like, a thin noodle type, plain tasty.
Rating (9/15): Plain tasty 😊　How about it when you come to Shintoshin for sightseeing and such?

さらばんじ.name: Sarabanji
さらばんじ.desc: A shop on Nago City's east coast, along National Route 331, near Kanucha Bay Resort. A light, gentle bonito broth with medium-thin noodles, and the complimentary small side dishes (kimchi and kubu irichi) are a nice touch too.
t: It was introduced in the "Nago City Soba Map", and I ate here in February 2021 😄
"Sarabanji" along National Route 331 on the east coast side of Nago City
"Sarabanji" introduced as shop 18 of 41 in the "Nago Soba Map"
I ordered the "Soki Soba" introduced in the map
Braised Pork Belly Soba　¥650 (I was supposed to have ordered soki soba but the "Braised Pork Belly Soba" came ^^;)

I was supposed to have ordered "Soki Soba"... but the "Braised Pork Belly Soba" came ^^;　Thinking "Oh well~", I just ate it as is lol　Bonito-stock broth with medium-thin noodles. A light type of broth with a gentle taste. The complimentary small side dishes of kimchi and kubu irichi (stir-fried shredded kelp) were delicious too.

Rating (9/15): "Kanucha Bay Resort" is also nearby, so how about it when you're staying there, driving along the east coast of northern Okinawa Island, or sightseeing? When I checked, it seems they have an Instagram too, so please check it out 😄

すば処月桃.name: Suba-dokoro Getto
すば処月桃.desc: A shop with an additive-free stock of ma-kombu kelp, bonito and pork bone, and homemade wood-ash noodles. The smooth, rich pork bone broth is high-level. The specialty is the Shishimai Suba topped with braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) and bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki).
t: I ate here in November 2023. This shop was a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1–2024.2.29)", and I went as my 23rd of 34 shops 😊
Suba-dokoro Getto (on the 1st floor of a building that looks like a JA building)
This shop wasn't a standalone house; it seemed to be in the 1st floor of a building-like structure. Judging from the address, maybe it's a JA building?
It was lunchtime on a holiday, but when I opened the door and went in, it was completely full (*_*)　I thought this must be a shop really loved by local customers.
But since it's Okinawa soba, I figured turnover would be fast and decided to wait a little. Then several groups left, so I made it inside safely 🤗

For my order, I got the "Shishimai Soba (rich)" introduced in the stamp rally booklet. When I said to the staff, "Nikumai soba, rich please," pointing at the booklet, they replied, "Shishimai soba, rich, right."　I had the reading wrong. In Okinawan dialect, meat is "shishi" (;^ω^)　My apologies lol
Menu
Menu
Menu (explanation part)
While waiting I checked the menu. Apparently these are homemade noodles made using the supernatant of wood ash (lye).
Wood-ash noodles may be a first for me since I had "hijaa (goat) soba" at "Mukashi Mukashi" in Nago.
However, even after a while since ordering, it just wouldn't come; at other shops, even when full, it comes in a reasonable time, but at this shop it just didn't come (;^ω^)
It seems the operation is being run by 2 elderly women, which is tough (;^ω^)
Shishimai Suba (rich) (medium)　¥890
Shishimai Suba (rich) (medium)　¥890

It finally came. First, the broth of course. According to the explanation, the broth: "We carefully make the stock with Hokkaido ma-kombu kelp, bonito and pork bone. The additive-free stock has a deeply nourishing flavor where you can feel savoriness that spreads naturally in your mouth and a powerful richness." 😁

Taking a sip, the rich pork bone stock comes through. It's smooth; I think it's richer and more delicious than the agu-stock Kame Soba or the rich pork bone stock of "Tsukikuruchi" I ate the day before. However, the saltiness is also on the strong side.
I think the broth is smooth, rich and delicious, but as expected it can't beat "796 Nankuru", which I introduce as a recommended shop 😊

Next I have the noodles. They're a medium-thin straight type. According to the explanation, "The homemade wood-ash noodles have a good aroma, and you can feel a springy chewiness, smooth texture going down, and a faint sweetness."
However, when I ate them, I couldn't feel the aroma or flavor of wood ash, and I think the ones I ate before at "Mukashi Mukashi" in Nago City had more flavor.
However, the noodles themselves are smooth and I think plain tasty. These noodles also come across a bit salty.
The toppings have volume with braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) and bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), but the hon-soki had a bit of sinewy texture and felt dry.

Rating (9.5/15): Plain tasty. The pork bone broth is fairly smooth and delicious, but a bit on the salty side. The noodles are smooth and plain tasty too, but these also come across salty. The operation when it's full is a bit disappointing.

そばcafeホウオウボク.name: Soba cafe Hoouboku
そばcafeホウオウボク.desc: A shop in Sokei, Ginoza Village, whose charm is a peaceful atmosphere where time seems to stand still. The signature is the good-value Hoouboku Soba with a chicken, pork and bonito stock broth, thick curly noodles, and jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) included. There are outdoor seats and 2nd-floor seats too, so you can spend your time yonna-yonna (slowly, slowly).
t: I ate here in November 2023. This shop was a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1–2024.2.29)", and I went as my 20th of 34 shops 😊
Soba cafe Hoouboku (it's in a very peaceful place 😊)
Soba cafe Hoouboku (it's in a very peaceful place 😊)
There are outdoor seats too 😁
This time I ate on the 1st floor, but there seems to be a 2nd floor too.
This shop is in a place called Sokei, Ginoza Village (Ginoza-son Sokei), and it's in a very peaceful location 🤗
When I went, I also felt an atmosphere like time had somehow stopped 😊　It made me feel like, in life, you don't have to rush so much; yonna-yonna (slowly, slowly) is fine lol

It was lunchtime on a weekday, but when I went in there was no one there. The relaxed feel is nice lol　When you enter the front door there's a meal ticket machine, and I ordered the "Hoouboku Soba" introduced in the stamp rally booklet.
Menu (I ordered the Hoouboku Soba introduced in the stamp rally, and it seems jushi comes with it too. What a good deal 🤗)

Seeing the meal ticket machine in front of the entrance, I thought "Cash only, huh," bought my meal ticket from the machine with cash and handed it in at the counter inside, but lo and behold, there was a PayPay QR code reader barcode placed there (;^ω^)　If they accept cashless too, I wish they'd let people know at the entrance (;^ω^)　I probably could have paid with my smartphone, but since I'd already bought the meal ticket with cash, I handed in my Hoouboku Soba ticket without complaint (;^ω^)
Hoouboku Soba (with jushi)　¥850
After a while, the "Hoouboku Soba" I ordered came 😊　Including jushi is great service 😊　First, I taste the broth (lol)
As the menu says, the stock broth using chicken, pork and bonito is a broth where the pork bone comes through somewhat.
Hoouboku Soba (with jushi)　¥850

Next I have the noodles. They're thick curly noodles with a soft feel, and since jushi comes with it too, the volume is full marks. The fish cake (kamaboko) is a topping not found at other shops, with a kind of Okinawan celebratory feel 🤗

Rating (9/15): It's an Okinawa soba shop where you can eat in a mellow atmosphere, at a location where time really seems to have stopped 😊　I recommend it to those who want to eat Okinawa soba leisurely in that kind of atmosphere. How about trying it once?

そば家幸.name: Sobaya Sachi
そば家幸.desc: In Kanna, Ginoza Village, marked by a warehouse-like exterior along National Route 329. A rare shop open only on Saturdays and Sundays, its interior is packed with pro baseball goods such as the Yomiuri Giants. The signature dish is the Sachi Soba with a blended broth where the richness of pork bone comes through. They also ship soba.
t: *This article was created with "ChatGPT 4o" with some additions by me. I went to eat here in January 2025 😄
This time again, in search of Okinawa soba, I drove north and further north, and where I ended up was "Sobaya Sachi" in Kanna, Ginoza Village. It has a rugged, warehouse-like exterior 😄

The moment you step inside, uniforms and goods from pro baseball's Yomiuri Giants and others are displayed all over the walls, with huge impact ⚾️✨

This shop is a rare one, open "only on Saturdays and Sundays". This time I visited at lunchtime on a Saturday, and cars kept pulling into the parking lot one after another; it was full of local customers and people who seemed to be tourists. Inside there are several table seats, with a relaxed, calm feel. There are also lots of players' autographs and photos on the walls, making it an irresistible space for baseball fans 📸

Now, what I ordered this time was the "Sachi Soba", which shares the shop's name. There were several kinds on the menu, but first I'm going with the signature dish~ 🍜
Sachi Soba (large)　¥950

The bowl that was brought out has a very Okinawan yachimun-style design, and just the look of it gets me excited 🎵　In addition to braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) and bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), there's fish cake (kamaboko) on top too, so it has quite a lot of volume. First, a sip of the broth… yep, a blended stock with the richness of pork bone gently coming through, and the saltiness is a bit strong. My impression is that rather than the light type, it's the solid type of broth.
Sachi Soba (large)　¥950
The noodles are medium-thick straight noodles, glossy in appearance ✨　Boiled on the soft side.

And then the meats… first, the bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki). These are surprisingly lightly seasoned, and rather than melt-in-your-mouth, they have a firm texture where the fibers remain. Quite a lot of sinew. The braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) also has a somewhat strong sinewy texture.

Rating (9/15): All in all, it feels plain tasty 👍　Even if you're not a baseball fan you can enjoy it, but it's a shop I'd really like you to visit once when you come to the northern region during camp season. You might be a little overwhelmed by the number of uniforms and photos on display (lol)
